title: Probability
summary: Dependent and independent events, the addition and product rules, mutually exclusive and complementary events, Venn diagrams, tree diagrams and contingency tables.

notes.latex: P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \text{ and } B)
notes.caption: The addition rule (inclusion–exclusion)

items: **Mutually exclusive** events cannot happen together: $P(A \text{ and } B) = 0$, so $P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B)$.
**Independent** events: the outcome of one does not affect the other, so $P(A \text{ and } B) = P(A) \times P(B)$.
**Dependent** events: the first outcome changes the probability of the second (e.g. drawing without replacement).

notes.title: Worked example 1: testing independence
notes.problem: $P(A) = 0{,}4$, $P(B) = 0{,}5$ and $P(A \text{ and } B) = 0{,}2$. Are A and B independent? Find $P(A \text{ or } B)$.
steps: $P(A) \times P(B) = 0{,}4 \times 0{,}5 = 0{,}2 = P(A \text{ and } B)$, so A and B are independent.

notes.title: Worked example 3: without replacement
notes.problem: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue sweets. Two are taken one after the other without replacement. Find $P(\text{one of each colour})$.

notes.caption: Survey of 200 learners: do they eat breakfast?

notes.text: $P(\text{Grade 10}) = 0{,}5$, $P(\text{breakfast}) = 0{,}6$ and $P(\text{Grade 10 and breakfast}) = \frac{60}{200} = 0{,}3 = 0{,}5 \times 0{,}6$. So eating breakfast is **independent** of grade in this survey.

questions.prompt: A and B are mutually exclusive with $P(A) = 0{,}3$ and $P(B) = 0{,}45$. Find $P(A \text{ or } B)$.
A and B are independent, $P(A) = 0{,}6$ and $P(B) = 0{,}3$. Find $P(A \text{ and } B)$.
If $P(A) = 0{,}2$, $P(B) = 0{,}5$ and $P(A \text{ and } B) = 0{,}15$, then A and B are independent.
In a class of 30, 18 take Science, 15 take Art and 6 take both. (a) Draw a Venn diagram. (b) How many take neither? (c) Find $P(\text{Science only})$.
The probability that a bus is late is 0,2 each day, independently. Find the probability that over two days the bus is (a) late on both days (b) late on exactly one day.
A box has 4 green and 6 yellow balls. Two are drawn without replacement. Find $P(\text{both green})$.
Of 150 people, 90 own a car. Of the car owners, 54 are employed full-time; 60 of the 150 are employed full-time. Is owning a car independent of full-time employment? Show working.
questions.memo:
✓ $P(\text{car}) \times P(\text{employed}) = 0{,}6 \times 0{,}4 = 0{,}24$ (1)
✓ $P(\text{car and employed}) = \frac{54}{150} = 0{,}36$ (1)
✓ Not equal, so the events are dependent (1)
